statement.p: Check that the point (-1,-1,1) lies on the given surface. Then, viewing the surface as a level surface for a function f(x,y,z), find a vector normal to the surface and an equation for the tangent plane to the surface at (-1,-1,1).

static.solution: 4(-1)^2 - 3(-1)^2 + 2(1)^2 = 3. Then let f(x,y,z) = 4x^{2}-3y^{2}+2z^{2} so that the given surface is the level surface f(x,y,z) = 3. Since f_x = 8x, f_y = -6y, and f_z = 4z, we have \mbox{grad} f(-1,-1,1) = -8\,\mathit{\vec i}+6\,\mathit{\vec j}+4\,\mathit{\vec k} Since gradients are perpendicular to level surfaces, a vector normal to the surface at (-1,-1,1) is \vec n=-8\vec i + 6\vec j + 4\vec k. Thus an equation for the tangent plane is 6\mathopen{}\left(y+1\right)-8\mathopen{}\left(x+1\right)+4\mathopen{}\left(z-1\right) = 0, or z = 1-\frac{6\mathopen{}\left(y+1\right)-8\mathopen{}\left(x+1\right)}{4}.
